note: Re-judged 2026-11-03 by an independent auditor who authored none of 816ce1ce4c, 2cbd255ba4, 2e5c2d012a, d22b811ce4 or 1a2ccaeef8 (phase 5 of spec-filter-wire-0-umbrella, the per-peer text filter chain deleted). RFC 4271 Section 9.2 read: "If a BGP speaker receives overlapping routes, the Decision Process MUST consider both routes based on the configured acceptance policy." Both tagged units moved through receiveOverlappingRoutes only: The test filter is now an answerTransport behind filterTransportSeam, compiled by answerPolicy into a policychain library chain, so the verdict travels the real filter-update path (route.Input, rpc.FilterUpdateOutput decoded by the library chain) instead of the deleted policyFilterSeam that handed a PolicyResponse straight to the text chain; that is the production path every plugin filter now takes. The filter reads prefix, and the received WireUpdate now carries a registered ASN4 receive context so the prefix read can decode the NLRI, as every received UPDATE does. Positive: the acceptance policy is asked twice and both 10.0.0.0/8 and 10.1.0.0/24 are dispatched in order. Negative: the policy rejects when the fields name 10.1.0.0/24, and only the /8 is dispatched; a fields read that missed the prefix would accept both and fail the exact-equality assertion, so the negative still discriminates on the policy verdict. Assertions unchanged; the residual noted before (verdict supplied by a test filter, not a parsed filter config) stands.
